summary: Iteration 5 validates the new XGBoost calibration layer end-to-end. Backend trains cleanly at import (no tracebacks). Updated pytest suite (7 tests) all pass. /api/overview.calibration now returns real learned metrics (accuracy=96.4, confidence=0.91, mae=3.57, r2=0.91, top_feature=rule_risk, 675 training / 225 test samples, version xgb-0.9.1) with a valid 6-feature importance dict summing to ~1.0. Every route now carries a calibrated_risk in [0,100] plus rainfall & wind. /api/reports response now includes calibrated_risk on the mutated route and the alert string contains 'calibrated'. Meghalaya High-severity report keeps calibrated_risk >= pre-report value (no regression). Alt-route switcher and vehicle reroute regression tests still green. Frontend Prediction Engine panel renders data-testid='model-meta' with real values (rule_risk / ±3.57 / 675 rows) — no hardcoded 89% or v0.8.4 present. Dashboard load, alerts, map, and switch-route UI all render without JS errors.
critical_code_review_comments: risk_model.py caches a single sklearn model in a module-level dict; fine for demo but not thread-safe if the app ever moves off Uvicorn single-worker.

server.py mutates the shared `routes` list on every /api/overview call (re-writing calibrated_risk in place). Harmless today, but concurrent reports + overview reads could race. Consider computing per-request copies.
The alert string in POST /api/reports hardcodes '2 vehicles rerouted' regardless of actual reroute count — cosmetic, but misleading if state has 0 or 1 vehicles.
seed_data_creation: None. Tests mutate in-memory fixtures (Assam + Meghalaya risk/incidents bumped by report tests).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend fixtures are in-memory and will drift each run — Assam route.risk grows by +18, Meghalaya by +18 (both capped at 98) per full test pass; rainfall also creeps up. If future assertions rely on absolute risk values, snapshot pre-report state first (as test_field_report_spikes_risk_and_reroutes_vehicle does). XGBoost training happens at server.py import (~600ms); a supervisor restart of backend triggers it — subsequent /api/overview calls are cheap batch predictions.
